title: PagedAttention (canonical fragmentation answer)

fields.detail: The canonical statement that block-paged KV management near-eliminates fragmentation waste. Verbatim from the abstract: "we propose PagedAttention, an attention algorithm inspired by the classical virtual memory and paging techniques in operating systems. On top of it, we build vLLM, an LLM serving system that achieves (1) near-zero waste in KV cache memory and (2) flexible sharing of KV cache within and across requests to further reduce memory usage." Retained as the canonical reference because the "is paging the right primitive" question is still live (see CLOSED-12 / ABANDONED-7).

title: Hybrid KV cache manager — single pool, many attention types

fields.detail: The shipped design for one shared pool across heterogeneous layer types. Verbatim: "We use a single memory pool for all layer types. The memory pool is split into multiple blocks with the same page size." The doc defines the three coordinators and states the shipped constraint verbatim: "**HybridKVCacheCoordinator**: Handles exactly two KV cache groups (must include one full‑attention group plus one other efficient‑attention group). Other cases are not implemented. You can disable prefix caching to use the KVCacheCoordinatorNoPrefixCache." Confirmed in the 0.29.0 tree: `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:591 class HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, plus `UnitaryKVCacheCoordinator` and `KVCacheCoordinatorNoPrefixCache`.

title: Decouple kernel block size from KV page size

fields.detail: Merged PR #24486 ("[Hybrid]: Decouple Kernel Block Size from KV Page Size", author zhiyuan1i) closed issue #24280. The issue framed the problem verbatim: "in hybrid mamba/attention models the `KVCacheManager` requires the mamba and attention page sizes to match, which might cause large attention page sizes (672 tokens for nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2). On the other hand, the FlashInfer attention backend uses TRTLLM FMHA kernels for Blackwell, which require page size up to 128". The closing confirmation comment on #24280 reads verbatim: "Thanks @zhiyuan1i for merging #24486 :) I can confirm this solves the issue for nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2". The 0.29.0 tree still carries the resulting machinery: `kernel_block_size` in `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:264` with the assertion "Kernel block size {bs} must divide KV cache block size {spec.block_size}."

title: Partial (sub-block) prefix cache hits for hybrid models

fields.detail: RFC #45702 "[RFC]: Partial Cache Hits for Hybrid Models" is `stateReason=COMPLETED` (closed as completed), i.e. implemented. It states the problem verbatim: "For hybrid full-attention + Mamba models, the full-attention block size needs to be aligned with the Mamba state block size. This makes block size super large compared to before. Since vLLM prefix-cache matching is block-size granular, this coarse block size leads to suboptimal cache hit rates." and "This RFC proposes separating prefix-cache matching granularity from block size granularity. We introduce hash_block_size to allow to hit a partial cache block." The 0.29.0 tree confirms shipment: `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:84 hash_block_size: int,` and the validation "assert scheduler_block_size % hash_block_size == 0".

title: Page-size unification / padding for heterogeneous layer types (the shipped allocator path)

fields.detail: The retrieved raw source of the shipped allocator contains the unification path. `def unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size(` is at line 1365 of the retrieved copy, and its docstring says verbatim: "If not same, unify the page size by increasing the block size of layers with smaller page size. Two cases cannot be unified by block size alone and pad their physical page to the maximum instead: Mamba layers, whose page size comes from state shapes and is independent of block size; and non-MLA attention layers whose page does not evenly divide the maximum (the padded page is read through a strided view)." The retrieved file contains 11 occurrences of `page_size_padded`, including the Mamba branch that pads to the maximum page. Scope limit, stated plainly: this row covers the **padding/alignment** path only. Exact per-layer (heterogeneous) page sizes are still proposed by the open PR #56156 ("It lets hybrid attention/state-cache models retain exact per-layer page sizes using vLLM's existing packed UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs allocator instead of padding every layer to one physical page size"), and its prerequisite #56155 is also still OPEN. Do not read this row as "heterogeneous page sizes are solved".

title: vAttention — contiguous virtual memory instead of paging

fields.detail: The canonical published counter-position to PagedAttention, still the reference for the "do we need paging" question. Verbatim from the abstract: "in trying to allocate physical memory at runtime, PagedAttention ends up changing the virtual memory layout of the KV cache from contiguous to non-contiguous. Such a design leads to non-trivial programming and performance overheads." and "vAttention is a simpler, portable, and performant alternative to PagedAttention: it supports various attention kernels out-of-the-box and improves LLM serving throughput by up to 1.23x compared to the use of PagedAttention-based kernels of FlashAttention and FlashInfer."

title: Minima-KV — mixed-format paged attention on the exact target GPU

fields.detail: Published mixed-format paging result evaluated on the target researcher's exact accelerator class. Verbatim from the abstract: "Across separate, configuration-bound Qwen3.6-27B profiles on a single 96-GB NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, deployment accounting reports 18.3 KiB of attention KV per live token, corresponding to 3.50x compression relative to BF16 and 1.75x relative to FP8." Mechanism verbatim: "Recent and protected Anchor pages remain in FP8, while older non-anchor pages move to packed TQ3; every live-request page remains addressable. Format-specific kernels compute partial attention states and combine them through a globally normalized online-softmax merge, enabling direct heterogeneous decode without a cache-sized dense shadow."

title: Per-group (decoupled) page size for Mamba/attention hybrids — fp8 KV cache yields no capacity gain

fields.who is still asking: vLLM issue #55196 (RFC), open
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` roughly doubles KV cache capacity on attention-only models (measured 2.00x), but on Mamba/GDN + attention hybrids it gives 1.84x at 32k context and 1.00x (no gain) at short context." and "Root cause is the known hybrid page-pinning behavior (#37121, #40696): the Mamba state is not quantized by `--kv-cache-dtype` and all groups share one uniform page, so the bf16 Mamba page pins bytes-per-block and the fp8 attention page cannot shrink the pool." and "Fix is parity work: quantize the Mamba state too (SGLang already does this at int8) and/or decouple per-group page size (SGLang/TRT-LLM/llama.cpp already use separate pools)."
fields.what specifically is missing: a per-group page size (or quantized Mamba state) in vLLM. The RFC states the mechanical blocker verbatim: "`get_uniform_page_size` asserts one page across all groups". No merged PR implements per-group pools.

title: Hybrid block sizes can invert the hash/block relationship and crash the offload connector

fields.who is still asking: vLLM issue #56396, open
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "Note `block_size (8) < hash_block_size (32)` — the call asks `resolve_block_hashes` to view 32-token-granularity hashes at a *finer* 8-token granularity, but the function only supports the coarsening direction (`block_size >= hash_block_size`, enforced by the divisibility assert). With 8 < 32 the assert `8 % 32 == 0` can never hold, so the crash is deterministic on the first request."
fields.what specifically is missing: support for a per-group block size smaller than the global `hash_block_size` (the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash layout has "MLA full-attention group @ block_size 32 + SWA/circular-buffer group @ block_size 8"). An open fix PR exists (#56404) but issue #56396 is open.

title: Naive round-robin block allocation for sliding-window layers — explicitly designed out

fields.who: vLLM maintainers, in the shipped hybrid KV cache design doc
fields.closure status: **"by design"** — the technique was considered and deliberately not adopted. This is a closed design decision, not a merged feature.
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "For sliding window attention layers, a naive implementation for memory allocation is to allocate `sliding_window_size` blocks and fill in the blocks in a round-robin way. But this naive implementation is not compatible with prefix caching so we didn't pick this design. In vLLM, we allocate different blocks for different tokens and free blocks that are outside the sliding window."
fields.date: doc states it was written against commit `458e74` (the doc carries no date in the retrieved copy; the linked commit is the reference point)
fields.note: the same doc records a second, softer abandonment of the current approach's quality, verbatim: "This case happens in Gemma-3 series models, and models in case 2 but with eagle speculative decoding which introduce one full attention layer. The solution has some memory waste and is not perfect. Please report any cases where padding overhead becomes unacceptable so we can refine the algorithm."

title: HMA is preserved by default for connectors that support it

fields.detail: PR #41847 (author chfeng-cs, title "[KV Transfer] Enable HMA by default for connectors that support it") is confirmed merged on the GitHub page and is visible in the local tree as `KVConnectorFactory.supports_hma_config`. The design was worked out in issue #41830, where the author wrote: "My plan is to add a config-level helper that resolves effective HMA support from KVTransferConfig, recursing into MultiConnector children, then use that in the auto-disable path." The shipped code was re-verified on live `main` at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/vllm/config/vllm.py (lines 2018-2024): `# Auto-disable HMA only when the connector config does not support it.` and `if not KVConnectorFactory.supports_hma_config(self.kv_transfer_config):`. Its warning text states the consequence: "hybrid SSM models (e.g. Jamba, Bamba) require HMA and will fail at startup without it; models with sliding window attention will run with reduced performance."

title: `kv_load_failure_policy` ships defaulting to `fail`, and is documented

fields.detail: The NixlConnector Usage Guide carries a "KV Load Failure Policy" section stating: "`fail` (default): Immediately fail the request with an error when KV load fails. This may cause performance `jitter` on decode instances..." The shipped default was re-verified on live `main` at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/vllm/config/kv_transfer.py (line 103): `kv_load_failure_policy: Literal["recompute", "fail"] = "fail"` with the docstring "'fail': immediately fail the request with an error finish reason (default)". It is also present in the local tree `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main`. The dedicated RFC that asked for this change, issue #32200, was nonetheless closed `NOT_PLANNED` by the stale bot — see ABANDONED-3.

title: Cross-topology P/D compatibility (hetero TP, block size, layout, dtype) is shipped and gated by a handshake hash

fields.detail: The compatibility matrix separates what must match from what may differ. "What must match between P and D — By default, a `compatibility hash` is checked during handshake. P and D instances must agree on: vLLM version and NIXL connector version, Model ..., Attention backend, KV cache dtype (`cache_dtype`), EAGLE/MTP-style speculative method ..., NIXL transfer mode (push vs pull) — a push (WRITE) connector and a pull (READ) connector use incompatible transfer protocols and must never be paired." "What can safely differ between P and D: `tensor-parallel-size` (heterogeneous TP ...), `block-size` (heterogeneous block size ...), Number of KV cache blocks ...". Layout defaults are stated: "NixlConnector defaults to `LBHNC` (head-major, formerly `HND`) layout for optimal transfer performance (non-MLA models)." Dynamic quantization is refused: "`Dynamic quantization` (scales computed at runtime): ❌ Not supported. Per-block scales are not transferred alongside KV cache data."

title: Prefill-vs-decode engine-count tuning has shipped, documented guidance

fields.detail: Dynamo's tuning guide has a section "Number of Prefill and Decode Engines" listing three load regimes and states: "At low load, disaggregation would not benefit much as prefill and decode are usually computed separately. It is usually better to use a single monolithic engine." It gives the ratio knob's direction explicitly: "Decrease the total amount of KV cache: Some GPUs are configured as prefill engines whose KV cache is not used in the decode phase. Since Dynamo currently allocates the KV blocks immediately when the decode engine get the requests, it is advisable to use as few prefill engines as possible (even no prefill engine) to maximize the available KV cache in decode engines." It also couples block size to transfer cost: "For block size, if the block size is too small, it leads to small memory chunks in the P->D KV cache transfer and poor performance... For most dense models, we find block size 128 is a good choice." And a live capability gap: "However, chunked prefill is currently not supported in Dynamo (vLLM backend)."

title: Reducing transferred bytes instead of overlapping transfer was published as a win under bandwidth constraints

fields.detail: SCD states the bottleneck premise plainly: "Disaggregated serving alleviates memory bottlenecks in Large Language Model (LLM) inference but creates a severe communication bottleneck: transmitting high-dimensional Key-Value (KV) caches often dominates time-to-first-token (TTFT)." Its result: "SCD delivers up to 2.65 × TTFT speedup over the oracle consumer prefill and dominates quantization and selective recomputation baselines on the quality--latency Pareto frontier in bandwidth-constrained regimes, while keeping generation quality within 5% F1 of the oracle." Its own limitation is stated in the abstract: reuse "across heterogeneous models (e.g. base and fine-tuned variants) causes semantic misalignment that accumulates over layers, degrading generation quality."

title: KV transfer failures are not reported to the scheduler for Mooncake P2P, so PD requests hang

fields.who is still asking: vLLM issue #55870 (reporter on Ascend A3 with MultiConnector + MooncakeConnector), and an open fix PR #56166 by LH-and-FPGA submitting on 2026-09-09
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "In the inspected implementation, discovery failure and per-request transfer errors appear to lack the scheduler-visible failure handling needed to unblock remote-KV waits."
fields.what specifically is missing: The scheduler is never notified of decode-side pull failures, so requests sit in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` until client timeout. The open PR #56166 describes the three dropping paths: "`_connect_to_prefiller_bootstrap()` does not propagate bootstrap failure to callers. `handle_new_engine_id()` bare-returns when the remote engine is unavailable, abandoning the pending `PullReqMeta` s. `process_pulling_result()` handles `ok_reqs` but only logs `err_reqs`." It notes the contrast: "NixlConnector already reports both handshake and transfer failures through this mechanism; Mooncake P2P was missing the equivalent wiring."

title: NIXL push-mode + pipeline parallelism is refused outright for hybrid (HMA) KV layouts, and HMA still opts out of block invalidation

fields.who is still asking: vLLM `NixlPushConnector` (ships a hard `NotImplementedError`), plus the residual HMA guard in the NIXL worker's failure path
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "NixlPushConnector does not support pipeline_parallel_size > 1 with hybrid KV cache layouts (HMA) yet." (raised in code as `raise NotImplementedError(...)` under `if self.pp_size > 1 and self._is_hma_required:`), immediately followed by a second refusal: "NixlPushConnector consumer (decode) does not support pipeline_parallel_size > 1."
fields.what specifically is missing: Two distinct gaps. (a) Push-mode NIXL cannot be combined with PP>1 on any hybrid (HMA) model. The in-code explanation is "PP push slices regions per layer (uniform count); HMA breaks that." (b) In the failure path, block invalidation is still conditioned on `if not self._is_hma_required:` inside `_report_failed_recv`, so on HMA-required models a failed receive is recorded and its handle released but no invalid block IDs are published to the scheduler.

title: An RFC to transfer last-token hidden states over the connector is closed but the capability is not in `KVConnectorBase_V1`

fields.who is still asking: vLLM issue #31064, filed for DeepSeek-R1 on Intel Gaudi/XPU
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "This RFC proposes an **optional, backward-compatible enhancement** to `KVConnectorBase_V1` (v1-only) to transfer **last-token hidden states** alongside KV cache under P/D disaggregation." and the motivating harm: "prefix-prefill injections introduce large step-time spikes (hundreds of milliseconds to seconds), these spikes directly inflate TPOT and tail ITL"
fields.what specifically is missing: The issue is marked CLOSED/COMPLETED, but the only hidden-states connector that ships is `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`, whose own docstring scopes it elsewhere: "Simple debug implementation of a HiddenStatesConnector. Simply extracts the hidden states from the kv cache and stores them to disk. Must be used in conjunction with the `extract_hidden_states` spec decoding method." That is a local-disk, speculative-decoding artifact — not the general P/D hidden-state transfer the RFC asked for. The maintainer pushback recorded on the issue was: "I have an aversion to adding this complexity in order to avoid running a single forward pass for 1 token --- so just want to make sure I understand why the current impl is not working well", and the closer: "Per offline discussion with @xinyu-intel, there is a lot of complexity here. On CUDA/ROCm, we currently do a single extra forward pass, but the passes are 'pure decode' ... On Gaudi plugin, even though there is only one token scheduled, the request is treated as a prefill. Gaudi team will look into improving this." So the question is resolved-as-wontfix-by-design on CUDA/ROCm, and re-opened as an open vendor-specific problem on Gaudi.

title: Bidirectional KV transfer's block-alignment guarantee breaks on stripped thinking traces

fields.who is still asking: vLLM NixlConnector Usage Guide "Limitations" section, with a cited open issue #43094
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "Reasoning models with stripped thinking traces — When using reasoning models (e.g. DeepSeek-R1) that produce thinking traces (`<think>...</think>`), D's KV blocks cover the full token sequence including thinking tokens. If the client strips thinking traces from the conversation history before sending the next turn, the prompt P receives will be missing tokens from the middle of what D generated. The block-alignment logic assumes P's prompt is a prefix of D's sequence, so pulling KV blocks from D in this case transfers cache computed for the wrong token positions, producing incorrect results."
fields.what specifically is missing: "We currently assume the router is able to detect such mismatch across turns." The correctness guarantee is pushed out of the engine into an unspecified external router. A second stated limitation is also open: host-buffer support "is planned for future work."

- Verbatim quote of the asking: "Reasoning models with stripped thinking traces — When using reasoning models (e.g. DeepSeek-R1) that produce thinking traces (`<think>...</think>`), D's KV blocks cover the full token sequence including thinking tokens. If the client strips thinking traces from the conversation history before sending the next turn, the prompt P receives will be missing tokens from the middle of what D generated. The block-alignment logic assumes P's prompt is a prefix of D's sequence, so pulling KV blocks from D in this case transfers cache computed for the wrong token positions, producing incorrect results."
- What specifically is missing: "We currently assume the router is able to detect such mismatch across turns." The correctness guarantee is pushed out of the engine into an unspecified external router. A second stated limitation is also open: host-buffer support "is planned for future work."
- Evidence: READ BODY

title: NIXL telemetry throughput conflates overlapped transfers and double-counts across TP ranks, so the KV bandwidth bottleneck cannot be measured correctly

fields.who is still asking: vLLM issue #33170 (reporter) — closed by the stale bot, never answered by a maintainer
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "here vLLM calculates the throughput by the `sum of bytes transferred /sum the xfer time`, but if there are multiple transfers overlapped, we can not simply sum each xfer time as the total duration. In real case, the total duration should be shorter if multiple transfers can be in parallel."
fields.what specifically is missing: A correct overlap-aware throughput definition, plus per-rank aggregation. A second reporter added: "it treats each rank as independent, so if total bytes_transferred is 1000MB and i have 8 ranks (tp=8), it treats each rank as 125MB and increase count by 8, instead of aggregating 1 transfer of 1000MB". Without this, the CLOSED-2 metric block cannot be used to size the transfer/compute overlap budget.

title: layerwise KV transfer in PD disaggregation (vLLM) — measured worse than bulk transfer, closed unmerged

fields.closure status: PR closed unmerged (state CLOSED, `"mergedTime": null`, `"mergedBy": null`), 2025-03-19T05:14:33Z
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "the layerwise method performs worse as it needs to retrieves layer_number tensors, so it requires more overhead. I will continue to work on the solution that the consumer starts to receive the KV cache once the producer completes a layer."
fields.evidence: READ BODY - Corroborating numbers from the same PR body, same page (all quoted verbatim from the PR description): the author posted both benchmarks. Layerwise: "Mean TTFT (ms): 167.27 Median TTFT (ms): 158.20 P99 TTFT (ms): 241.40". The PR was also a declared 2-GPU PyNccl design — `LayerwisePyNcclConnector` with `"kv_rank":0,"kv_parallel_size":2` on producer and `"kv_rank":1,"kv_parallel_size":2` on consumer — which independently puts the technique in HW_RULED_OUT territory.

title: Prefill-as-a-Service — cross-datacenter KV transport over commodity Ethernet between separate clusters

fields.hardware requirement: Multiple loosely coupled clusters across datacenters, with standalone compute-dense prefill clusters and local PD clusters, and an internal 1T-parameter hybrid model.
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "We present Prefill-as-a-Service (PrfaaS), a cross-datacenter serving architecture that selectively offloads long-context prefill to standalone, compute-dense prefill clusters and transfers the resulting KVCache over commodity Ethernet to local PD clusters for decode." and its evaluation: "In a case study using an internal 1T-parameter hybrid model, a PrfaaS-augmented heterogeneous deployment achieves 54% higher serving throughput and 64% lower P90 TTFT than a homogeneous PD baseline".
fields.relevance to this subsection: this is the boundary case that defines how far the KV-transfer-cost question can be pushed (cross-datacenter), and it needs a 1T-parameter model and multiple clusters. Its stated premise also confirms the CLOSED-8 framing: "in practice its deployment boundary is still determined by KVCache transfer."

title: SGLang chose a hard-error guard over fixing HiCache sidecar migration

fields.detail: The question "are HiCache host-tier hits safe with MoE routed_experts?" was answered "no, and we will fail fast rather than fix". Verbatim from `Cerdore`: "HiCache load_back relocates tokens to new slots without migrating that sidecar data, so a host-tier hit returns stale rows from whatever previously occupied the new slot. MoE is skipped on cache hits, so there's no recomputation to fix it." And: "Opened #27067 as a guard: hard error on the unsafe combo until the migration path lands. Auto-disabling either flag silently produces a different wrong result, so failing fast is the safer option." The issue itself was then closed `NOT_PLANNED` on 2026-07-10.

title: vLLM v1 KV cache offloading — the canonical open RFC

fields.who is still asking: `orozery` (author), `njhill`, `josephrocca`; open since 2025-06-19 and labelled `RFC`, `keep-open`
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "Currently, in vLLM v1 there is no in-house solution for offloading KV cache data from the GPU memory to other medium (in particular, CPU memory)." The break-even problem is stated by a maintainer in-thread — `njhill`: "Cached CPU blocks would't necessarily have all preceding blocks also in the CPU cache, some prefix might only reside in the GPU cache. For a given cache tier, we may some length threshold below which it's not worth retrieving (and therefore possibly also not worth storing) since it would be faster to recompute." `orozery` concedes the design implication: "I understand this may not be the case, and CPU size could be roughly the same size as the GPU, or larger by a small factor. So you make up a good point."
fields.what specifically is missing: an eviction-time (not compute-time) GPU→CPU save hook, and a decision on the GPU-block "next-in-line" notification — "since we want this to be async, this will require changes to vllm's core, allowing the connector to be notified on 'soon-to-be-evicted' GPU blocks." The thread ends without resolution.

title: SGLang HiCache load-back does not overlap the forward pass at all

fields.who is still asking: `qidaye`, filed 2026-09-08, still open
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "The consequence is that the layer-wise pipeline (`LayerDoneCounter` / `wait_until` in the attention layers) almost never overlaps anything: by the time `start_loading` returns and the batch is built and launched, every copy has already landed." … "So the scheduler thread stalls for the full enqueue duration, and the forward that should have hidden the H2D copies only starts once they are essentially complete." Measured table in the body: per-layer `load_to_device_per_layer` submission (CPU) `~2.4 ms`; `start_loading` per burst (78 layers x 2 pools) `~375 ms`; **"share of the H2D copy time that overlapped compute | 0.04 %"**.

title: LMCache CacheBlend — non-prefix reuse decays back to the cold baseline

fields.closure status: closed as not planned by a human, 2026-08-21, with only the terse comment "Closing here"
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "Once L1 saturates, LRU evicts the **warm document chunks** (the only thing the matcher can actually reuse), so the speedup **decays from a post-warm burst down to the cold baseline within a few dozen queries.** Nothing is functionally wrong; the store/lookup **asymmetry** is the defect. Production impact: any benchmark that re-warms before each measurement reports the burst (e.g. 4–6×) and completely misses that steady-state throughput under real sustained novel traffic falls back to ~1×." title: vLLM FP8 KV-cache — the measured failure modes before the fixes

fields.who: vLLM (AWS + Red Hat AI authors of the blog)
fields.closure status: published negative result, partially remediated; residual limits explicitly documented as "When to Avoid FP8 KV-Cache"
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "On Hopper GPUs, the FP8 Flash Attention 3 kernel suffered from accumulation precision loss at long contexts. On a 128k needle-in-a-haystack task, FP8 accuracy dropped from 91% (BF16 baseline) to just 13% — a regression traced to imprecise FP32 accumulation in the Tensor Cores". "The FP8 ITL slope for models with sliding-window attention layers (e.g., gpt-oss-20b) was nearly identical to BF16 (96% of BF16 slope), meaning users gained almost no decoding speedup despite halving memory. The break-even point exceeded 700k tokens — well beyond most practical context lengths." Residual: "for head dimensions larger than 128, the prefill performance remains behind BF16." And the explicit avoidance list: "FP8 KV-cache quantization is not always the right choice. Consider staying with BF16 if: Your contexts are short (< ~7k tokens): FP8 has a small constant overhead (the intercept gap), so at short contexts BF16 may be slightly faster for ITL. Your model uses head_dim = 256 and prefill latency matters: The two-level accumulation overhead increases TTFT by ~1.6x at long contexts." Quantified in their Table 3: `gpt-oss-20b before (v0.10.2) FP8 741,565 96%` break-even tokens and slope.

title: SGLang HiCache host hits returned stale MoE sidecar data

fields.closure status: closed as not planned 2026-07-10 (human-authored root-cause comment; the guard was shipped instead of the fix)
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "the routed_experts capturer (state_capturer/) indexes its buffer by device KV-pool slot. HiCache load_back relocates tokens to new slots without migrating that sidecar data, so a host-tier hit returns stale rows from whatever previously occupied the new slot. MoE is skipped on cache hits, so there's no recomputation to fix it. Plain radix cache is unaffected (slots stay in place). Same structural hazard in enable_return_indexer_topk." … "Opened #27067 as a guard: hard error on the unsafe combo until the migration path lands. Auto-disabling either flag silently produces a different wrong result, so failing fast is the safer option."

The closest genuine analogues are ABANDONED-17, -18, -22 (offload measures as pure overhead vs vLLM's own prefix cache) and ABANDONED-45 (PCIe-bound prefetching, but for MoE experts).

title: vLLM Context Parallel Deployment doc — the written multi-GPU contract

fields.detail: Merged 2025-10-15 by youkaichao ("add doc to explain the new DCP feature"). The doc is the canonical statement of why this technique class is multi-GPU by construction: "Say we have `N` GPUs, we can split the request into `N` chunks, and each GPU computes one chunk of the query/key/value tensors." It then makes DCP's dependency on TP explicit: "If one GPU cannot hold them all, or we want to hold more requests in the KV cache, we can first shard the KV cache along the `H` dimension, that's the plain tensor parallel sharding. It's as simple as adding `-tp <num_gpus>` to the command line." … "Then we need to add decode context parallel to further shard the KV cache along the `T` dimension. This is as simple as adding `-dcp <size>` to the command line. Note that `size` does not increase the number of GPUs we need to launch, but just reduces the KV cache duplication. The dcp size should lie in the range of `[1, tp_size/H]`." The doc also admits prefill CP was not finished at that point: "Both approaches are under active development." Its worked examples are all 8–16 GPU deployments: "For DeepSeek-R1, we have 1 kv-head when MLA is enabled. The typical single-node deployment with `-tp 8` causes 8x KV cache duplication. We can consider adding `-dcp 8` to reduce the KV cache duplication." … "When we deploy it with `-tp 16`, the KV cache duplication is 16x. We can add `-dcp 16` to completely remove the KV cache duplication". It credits the interleaving sharding idea to Moonshot and arXiv 2507.07120.

title: SGLang — shipped prefill context parallelism (`--enable-prefill-cp`, `--attn-cp-size`)

fields.detail: Shipped. The SGLang GLM-5.3 cookbook states: "Prefill context parallelism can help with reduction of TTFT under long context. To enable prefill context parallelism for GLM 5.3, please append the following arguments:" followed by the flags `--attn-cp-size 8`, `--enable-prefill-cp`, `--cp-strategy interleave`, and explains: "which splits the sequence equally across `--attn-cp-size` ranks during attention forward. The trade off for prefill CP is that it will introduce extra all-gather operation before indexer-topk and attention kernels, so it will increase latency for decode (in unified deployment) or short prefill." The referenced DeepSeek-V3.2 cookbook shows the same feature with `--cp-strategy interleave` and `--attn-cp-size 8` at "CP8", and a combined deployment path: "**PP + CP (multi-node):** Combines Pipeline Parallelism and Context Parallelism for cross-node scaling. The production-optimized configurations below have been verified on Hopper:" with the shipped multi-node invocation containing `--dist-init-addr ${prefill_master_ip}:5000`, `--nnodes 2`, `--node-rank 0`, `--tp-size 16`. The LayerSplit composition is described as: "With LayerSplit, the kv cache on each rank can be sharded over the CP attention group, and prefetched when necessary. This can reduce kv cache memory by up to 75%, thus increasing the throughput on prefill side."

title: SGLang — shipped decode context parallelism (`--dcp-size`) with an explicit MNNVL hardware gate

fields.detail: Shipped and documented. The page's own definition: "Decode context parallelism (DCP) stripes a request's MLA KV cache across ranks in an existing tensor-parallel group. With DCP size c, rank r owns position p when p mod c = r, so each rank stores and reads roughly 1/c of the cache." Its containment rule is a hard topology constraint: "A DCP group must fit inside one attention-TP group and one attention-DP replica: Topology / attn_tp_size = tp_size / attn_dp_size / attn_tp_size % dcp_size == 0. For example, TP=64, DP=4, DCP=16 creates four valid 16-rank attention replicas. DCP=32 would cross replica boundaries and is invalid." It also documents an unfixed validation gap: "Startup currently checks only tp_size % dcp_size == 0, not the stronger condition above. Until that check is fixed, DPA+DCP deployments must enforce containment when choosing the topology." The canonical multi-GPU example: "MLA decode on DeepSeek-V3.1 with DCP 8 inside TP 8: sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1 --trust-remote-code --tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8". And a 32-GPU example: "Kimi K3 on 32 GPUs with DPA and DCP 8. The model override enables replicated Q by default; the communication backend resolves generically to fi_a2a on MNNVL systems, otherwise a2a".

title: Helix Parallelism — KV parallelism during attention, published by NVIDIA

fields.detail: Published 2025-07-07, NVIDIA. Abstract: "We introduce Helix Parallelism, a hybrid execution strategy that applies KV parallelism during attention to shard KV caches across GPUs, then reuses the same GPUs for TP in dense LLMs or TP × Expert Parallel (EP) in MoEs during FFN computation." … "Compared to conventional parallelism approaches, Helix reduces TTL by up to 1.5x at fixed batch sizes and supports up to 32x larger batches under the same latency budget for DeepSeek-R1, pushing forward the throughput-latency Pareto on Blackwell". This is the paper vLLM's own CP deployment doc cites (arXiv 2507.07120) for DCP KV sharding, so it is the canonical reference for this cell. Critically for the hardware class, §3.1 Experimental setup says: "To evaluate the performance of different sharding strategies independent of potential feature gaps in a given software framework, we opt to leverage an in-house high-fidelity simulator modeling the latest GB200 hardware. The simulator accounts for both compute and communication costs, including latency from inter-GPU NVLink transfers, DRAM bandwidth constraints, and FLOP throughput. All performance numbers are normalized to that of the baseline to focus on the trends as opposed to specific performance claims." The evaluated models are also far outside one GPU: "(i) Llama-405B [12], a dense 405B parameter model with 128 query heads and 8 grouped KV heads (i.e., GQA attention). (ii) DeepSeek-R1 [13], a 671B parameter MoE model with MLA attention." and "we simulate decode-time inference with KV-cache sequence lengths of one million tokens and beyond."

title: Mooncake — KVCache-centric disaggregated architecture (multi-node canonical reference)

fields.url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00079 (full HTML v3: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.00079v3); shipped connector at `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main/docs/features/mooncake_connector_usage.md`
fields.detail: Published. Abstract: "Mooncake is the serving platform for Kimi, a leading LLM service provided by Moonshot AI. It features a KVCache-centric disaggregated architecture that separates the prefill and decoding clusters. It also leverages the underutilized CPU, DRAM, and SSD resources of the GPU cluster to implement a disaggregated cache of KVCache." The vLLM connector doc states the transport requirement verbatim: "Compared to traditional caching systems, Mooncake utilizes (GPUDirect) RDMA technology to transfer data directly in a zero-copy manner, while maximizing the use of multi-NIC resources on a single machine." and lists `device_name` as "Comma-separated whitelist of RDMA devices (e.g. `"mlx5_0,mlx5_1"`) to restrict topology discovery to. Empty discovers every device. Useful on hosts exposing a mix of InfiniBand and RoCE ports, where both peers must settle on the same link layer." The shipped vLLM example is a two-host deployment: "python examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py --prefill http://192.168.0.2:8010 --decode http://192.168.0.3:8020".

title: DistServe — disaggregating prefill and decoding

fields.detail: Published. Abstract: "DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences." §6.1 Experimental Setup is the canonical hardware statement: "Cluster testbed. We deploy DistServe on a cluster with 4 nodes and 32 GPUs. Each node has 8 NVIDIA SXM A100-80GB GPUs connected with NVLINK. The cross-node bandwidth is 25Gbps." The paper also states that even the intra-node fallback requires NVLink: "While many modern GPU clusters for LLMs are equipped with InfiniBand (e.g., 800 Gbps), in cases where cross-node bandwidth is limited, DistServe relies on the commonly available intra-node NVLINK, where the peak bandwidth between A100 GPUs is 600 GB/s, again rendering the transmission overhead negligible (see § 6.3)." The minimum viable unit in the paper's own Figure 1 framing is also >1 GPU: "Ideally, by allocating 2 GPUs for prefill and 1 GPU for decoding, we can effectively serve the model with an overall goodput of 10 rps, or equally 3.3 rps per GPU, which is 2.1x higher than existing systems."

title: Splitwise — phase splitting across separate machines

fields.detail: Published. Abstract: "we propose Splitwise, a model deployment and scheduling technique that splits the two phases of LLM inference requests on to separate machines. … Request state is transferred efficiently between machines using optimized network libraries on the fast back-plane interconnects available in today's GPU clusters." §V-A Experimental setup is the canonical hardware statement: "To evaluate our proposal on real hardware, we implement Splitwise's KV-cache transfer mechanism on top of vLLM [51]. Our implementation is open source [1]. We run this modified vLLM on two DGX-A100 and two DGX-H10 virtual machines (VMs) on Microsoft Azure with specifications from Table I. These are the VMs used to collect the characterization data in Section III. These machines are connected with InfiniBand and the DGX-H100s have double the bandwidth (i.e., 400 Gbps)." The KV transfer design is explicitly cross-machine (Section IV-C is titled "KV-cache transfer", IV-D "Provisioning with Splitwise"); the paper's own §IV-E states: "Since Splitwise is built solely by exploiting these phases, it is applicable to all of the current and upcoming LLMs, as long as the auto-regressive nature of the workflow requires these two phases." Its characterization runs also used 8-GPU machines: "Unless stated otherwise, we run BLOOM-176B and Llama-70B on vLLM [51] on a machine with 8 H100 [16] GPUs."

The configuration section states: "Configuration. We implement Star Attention using HuggingFace Transformers library (Wolf et al., 2020). All experiments are done on A100 GPUs with bfloat16 precision."

title: NVIDIA Dynamo — shipped multi-node inference orchestration with KV-aware routing and KVBM

fields.detail: Shipped (README retrieved 2026-09). Verbatim: "**The open-source, datacenter-scale inference stack.** Dynamo is the orchestration layer above inference engines — it doesn't replace SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or vLLM, it turns them into a coordinated multi-node inference system. The README's own "when to use this" filter is verbatim: "You're serving LLMs across **multiple GPUs or nodes** and need to coordinate them" and "If you're running a single model on a single GPU, your inference engine alone is probably sufficient." Its KV features are described as: "**KV Block Manager (KVBM)** | Offloads KV cache across GPU → CPU → SSD → remote storage | Extends effective context length beyond GPU memory" and "**ModelExpress** | Streams model weights GPU-to-GPU via NIXL/NVLink | 7x faster cold-start for new replicas" and "**Grove** | K8s operator for topology-aware gang scheduling (NVL72) | Places workloads optimally across racks, hosts, and NUMA nodes". Its headline performance number is also NVL72-only: "**7x** higher throughput per GPU | DeepSeek R1 on GB200 NVL72 w/ Dynamo vs B200 without".

title: Prefill Context Parallel for Qwen3.5 hybrid attention (full-attention + GatedDeltaNet linear attention)

fields.who is still asking: Yancey0623 — vLLM issue #37995 `[RFC]: Prefill Context Parallel for Qwen3.5 Hybrid Attention` (OPEN, created 2026-03-24; auto-marked stale 2026-06-27 but still open, not closed)
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "Long-context prefill is a major bottleneck for LLM inference: 1. **Quadratic attention complexity**: Full attention is O(N^2) in sequence length, making 256K+ contexts extremely slow 2. **Memory bandwidth** : Large KV caches stress memory subsystem — Tensor Parallelism (TP) helps by distributing model weights, but each GPU still processes the full sequence. Context Parallel (CP) addresses this by distributing the sequence itself across GPUs." - The author's own admission that the linear-attention half is unfinished: "Linear attention layers maintain a recurrent state that depends on all previous tokens, so naively splitting the sequence would break correctness. This can be parallelized using sequence parallelism designed for linear attention e.g. [Linear Attention Sequence Parallelism](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02882) However, full attention is the bottleneck for long context, this RFC prioritizes context parallel for full attention layers. I haven't done a deep dive into linear attention parallelization yet, but it's definitely on the roadmap."
fields.what specifically is missing: sequence parallelism for the GatedDeltaNet/linear-attention layers, and an implementation PR. The RFC is design-only: there is no merged code.

title: vLLM — pipeline parallelism halves the usable KV block budget; declined as by-design

fields.who: reporter (issue body), answered by andoorve (vLLM maintainer)
fields.closure status: **Closed as not planned** (`state_reason: NOT_PLANNED`) by the **stale bot** after the maintainer's substantive answer; the maintainer's answer is a human "this is by design" statement and is quoted below, so this row does have a genuine human reason even though the mechanical closure was automated.
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "This is kind of expected behavior based on what our implementation of PP aims to do. We report 1650 blocks because this is the total number of blocks available on your GPU. However, this gets divided into 2 KV cache sections to support multiple request streams at the same time. This is what allows us to have pipelining of request streams at the same time with load balancing of the two streams. This reporting could possibly be improved to reflect this." … "The situation you are talking about (very long prompt) is possible with some changes. You can submit a feature request for the same if there's a very clear use case for it. However, it wasn't a main focus until now since basically only 1 of those very long prompts could be resident in the cache at a time. This would mean essentially no pipelining, and you might want to see if tensor parallelism serves your use case better." The maintainer later restated it definitively: "So the halving is fundamental to the implementation here, whether you use 1 node or multiple the number of blocks per microbatch slot will be less compared to without pipeline parallelism."
fields.the reporter's measurement, verbatim: "Using `--pipeline_parallel_size=2`, it will throw an error if the prompt uses more than half the available tokens. … vLLM reports a capacity of 1650 blocks / 26.4k tokens when loading the model, `--max_model_len` was set to 24000 … But when sending any prompt with >13k tokens, it throws an `input prompt is too long` error".

title: vLLM docs — disaggregated prefill is documented as NOT a throughput win

fields.who: vLLM project (the docs page's own warning)
fields.closure status: **Shipped feature with an explicit negative scope statement** — the technique is published and supported, but the project states in its own docs that the headline benefit does not exist. This is a paper/doc-level negative result (Hard Rule 7).
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "!!! note Disaggregated prefill DOES NOT improve throughput."
fields.the feature is also gated as experimenta: "!!! note This feature is experimental and subject to change." and its implementation requires two instances by construction, verbatim: "We implement disaggregated prefilling by running 2 vLLM instances. One for prefill (we call it prefill instance) and one for decode (we call it decode instance), and then use a connector to transfer the prefill KV caches and results from prefill instance to decode instance." and "This feature is experimental and subject to change." - The vLLM NIXL connector docs additionally require RDMA for the transfer path, verbatim: "In standard disaggregated prefilling, KV cache flows in one direction: Prefill (P) computes the KV cache and Decode (D) reads from P." … "4. D reads KV blocks from P via RDMA (peer-to-peer pull), then generates the response." and a hardware caveat: "GB-series GPUs support multi-node NVLink. NIXL supports this capability, but KVCache must be registered as VMM during KVCache registration. To enable this feature, you need to set `--enable-cumem-allocator` or `--enable-sleep-mode` flags, and set `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL: 'y'` env. Otherwise, NIXL can only use RDMA/TCP for cross-node KVCache transfers."

title: "Beyond the Buzz: A Pragmatic Take on Inference Disaggregation" — disaggregation is not a universal solution

fields.closure status: **Published negative/limiting result** — the paper's headline finding undercuts the multi-node disaggregation technique for a large part of the design space.
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "As demonstrated in Figure 1, disaggregation is not a universal solution. In the following sections, we examine the performance benefits of disaggregated inference serving across a broad design space."
fields.abstract, verbatim: "As inference scales to multi-node deployments, disaggregation - splitting inference into distinct phases - offers a promising path to improving the throughput-interactivity Pareto frontier. Despite growing enthusiasm and a surge of open-source efforts, practical deployment of disaggregated serving remains limited due to the complexity of the optimization search space and system-level coordination. In this paper, we present the first systematic study of disaggregated inference at scale, evaluating hundreds of thousands of design points across diverse workloads and hardware configurations. We find that disaggregation is most effective for prefill-heavy traffic patterns and larger models." - Its NVLink-domain finding is directly hardware-relevant, verbatim: "Figure 11 shows the Pareto performance of disaggregated serving for two NVLink domain sizes. The analysis reveals that larger NVLink domains consistently enhance disaggregated serving performance. The benefit comes from the flexibility to choose wider expert and tensor parallelism during generation." and a scale caveat, verbatim: "A similar effect is expected in small-scale GPU deployments, where limited resources can restrict the rate matching search space."

title: Star Attention — distributed attention is SLOWER than ordinary single-machine inference below 32K

fields.who: NVIDIA (Acharya, Jia, Ginsburg), the paper's own Appendix C.1 / Table 6
fields.closure status: **Published result that undercuts the technique's own applicability range** (Hard Rule 7). The multi-host sharding scheme is a net loss for short and medium contexts, and the paper states this itself.
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "For sequence lengths below 32K, vanilla inference is faster than the distributed attention mechanisms, primarily due to the GPU communication overhead incurred in the distributed setups. However, in long context scenarios i.e. on sequence lengths exceeding 32K tokens, Star Attention begins to demonstrate clear performance advantages." - The paper's own Table 6 numbers make the loss concrete for Llama3.1-8B-Instruct: `16K → Vanilla 7s, Ring 10s, Star 9s`; `32K → Vanilla 10s, Ring 12s, Star 10s`; `64K → Vanilla 18s, Ring 22s, Star 12s`; `128K → Vanilla OOM, Ring 53s, Star 20s`. - The technique also permits accuracy loss by design, verbatim: "The choice of block size is dependent on the user on how much accuracy can be traded for improved speed." and the reported quality gap, verbatim: "Notably, Star Attention achieves scores nearly identical to global attention in Single-NIAH tasks. However, in more complex tasks such as Multi-NIAH and QA, it shows slight decline in performance, with reductions ranging from 1.6% to 4.9% in Multi-NIAH and 0.9% to 6.8% in QA tasks."

title: vLLM MoRIIO — multi-node TP16 prefill→decode KV dispatch fixed three times, all closed unmerged

fields.url: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45228 (plus predecessors/follow-ups #43063 and #45230, per an independent research sub-agent's retrieval)
fields.closure status: **PR closed unmerged** — superseded by three other PRs that did merge. The closer comment is a human statement, so this row has a substantive (non-bot) reason.
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "The issue that this PR targets has been addressed by #46116, #46115, and #47495, all of which have been merged. This PR can be safely closed."
fields.what it was fixing, verbatim from the pr: "MoRIIO advertised a single peer host per instance. That breaks TP prefill→decode once the peer's TP group spans more than one host: a decode worker whose matching prefill rank lives on the second host still points at the first one, handshakes and reads the wrong KV, and the request wedges. It shows up in TP16 1P1D across two hosts. Single-host and TP<=8 deployments never hit it."
fields.the multi-node-specific mechanism, verba: "An instance already knows the ordered host list of its own TP group; this PR reads it from kv_connector_extra_config[\"node_hosts\"] and publishes it at worker registration." … "n_hosts = len(remote_hosts) ranks_per_node = tp_size // n_hosts # 16 // 2 = 8 host = remote_hosts[tp_rank // ranks_per_node] In TP16 over two hosts, ranks 0–7 resolve to remote_hosts[0] and ranks 8–15 to remote_hosts[1]." - A sub-agent additionally recorded that the two predecessor PRs (#43063, #45230) carried the same failure signature and quotes from those pages: "…every decode rank dials a single remote_host parsed from request_id, which always resolves to the prefill head… the subsequent MoRI-IO RDMA read never completes, and the engine wedges at shm_broadcast.py:698". Those two bodies I did not personally open.

fields.who: vllm-agent (author of the revert PR), 1 commit
fields.closure status: **Revert PR closed unmerged** in favour of a narrower fix; the substantive statement is in the PR body itself, plus the terminal comment "A narrower fix is now available in #54400 ." — a human/automated-agent technical reason, not a stale timer.
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "The regression is one gated assignment. In SparseAttnIndexer.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size , the memoization is conditional: if isinstance ( get_forward_context (). attn_metadata , dict ): self . _cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = value return value When attn_metadata is not a dict , the value is never cached, so every subsequent forward re-enters get_current_vllm_config() . Outside a set_current_vllm_config() context that raises. Caching unconditionally on first access — or resolving the value eagerly in Worker.initialize_from_config , as the docstring says already happens — should fix this without a revert. If a maintainer lands that, please close this PR."

title: vLLM Decode Context Parallel (DCP) for GQA/MQA — hard-coded rejection unless TP exceeds the model's KV-head count

fields.hardware requirement: **More than one GPU, and specifically `--tensor-parallel-size` strictly greater than the model's total number of KV heads.** For a GQA model with 8 KV heads (the Qwen3 family shape) this means TP ≥ 9, i.e. **at least 9 GPUs**; the DCP size must additionally divide TP, so in practice 16 GPUs.

title: vLLM DCP — structurally a re-partition of an existing TP group, so it cannot exist on one GPU

fields.hardware requirement: **More than one GPU** (DCP never adds ranks; it subdivides the TP group, therefore `tp_size > 1` is a precondition).
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "tp_size needs to be divisible by dcp_size, because the world size does not change by dcp, it simply reuse the GPUs of TP group, and split one TP group into tp_size//dcp_size DCP groups." (PR #23734 body)
fields.the doc's framing, verbatim: "If one GPU cannot hold them all, or we want to hold more requests in the KV cache, we can first shard the KV cache along the `H` dimension, that's the plain tensor parallel sharding. It's as simple as adding `-tp <num_gpus>` to the command line." … "Then we need to add decode context parallel to further shard the KV cache along the `T` dimension. This is as simple as adding `-dcp <size>` to the command line. Note that `size` does not increase the number of GPUs we need to launch, but just reduces the KV cache duplication. The dcp size should lie in the range of `[1, tp_size/H]`." - The doc's single-GPU case is explicitly "do nothing", verbatim: "1. If one GPU can hold them all, and the performance is good enough, then no parallelization is needed."

title: SGLang DCP — the lowest-latency backend has a hard MNNVL/Blackwell gate

fields.hardware requirement: **Blackwell GPUs, with the whole DCP group inside one MNNVL domain — i.e. GB200/GB300 fabric, or a single multi-GPU node.** The DCP group must additionally be contained in one attention-TP group and one attention-DP replica.
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "fi_a2a, replicated Q | One FlashInfer MNNVL A2A | Requires Blackwell and a DCP group inside one MNNVL domain (GB200/GB300 fabric, or a single node)"
fields.topology requirement, verbatim: "A DCP group must fit inside one attention-TP group and one attention-DP replica: Topology / attn_tp_size = tp_size / attn_dp_size / attn_tp_size % dcp_size == 0. For example, TP=64, DP=4, DCP=16 creates four valid 16-rank attention replicas. DCP=32 would cross replica boundaries and is invalid."
fields.definitional requirement, verbatim: "Decode context parallelism (DCP) stripes a request's MLA KV cache across ranks in an existing tensor-parallel group."
fields.documented example topologies, verbatim: "MLA decode on DeepSeek-V3.1 with DCP 8 inside TP 8: sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1 --trust-remote-code --tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8" and "Kimi K3 on 32 GPUs with DPA and DCP 8." - Its DCP × PD-disaggregation composition adds a further transport requirement, verbatim: "This composition requires Mooncake or NIXL, matching physical page size and KV dtype, prefill attention CP 1, and decode chunk cache. Decode radix cache and HiCache are not supported here."

title: Helix Parallelism — evaluated on GB200 NVL72, via simulator with inter-GPU NVLink, on 405B/671B models

fields.hardware requirement: **GB200 NVL72-class hardware with inter-GPU NVLink; models of 405B and 671B parameters; KV histories of ≥1M tokens.** The evaluation is a simulator of GB200, not a single-GPU run.
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "To evaluate the performance of different sharding strategies independent of potential feature gaps in a given software framework, we opt to leverage an in-house high-fidelity simulator modeling the latest GB200 hardware. The simulator accounts for both compute and communication costs, including latency from inter-GPU NVLink transfers, DRAM bandwidth constraints, and FLOP throughput. All performance numbers are normalized to that of the baseline to focus on the trends as opposed to specific performance claims."
fields.model scale, verbatim: "We evaluate Helix Parallelism on two large-scale LLMs representative of dense and MoE architectures: (i) Llama-405B [12], a dense 405B parameter model with 128 query heads and 8 grouped KV heads (i.e., GQA attention). (ii) DeepSeek-R1 [13], a 671B parameter MoE model with MLA attention. In MLA, key and value projections are absorbed into a latent space during decoding and are not explicitly materialized, effectively resulting in a single KV head shared across all 128 query heads." and "we simulate decode-time inference with KV-cache sequence lengths of one million tokens and beyond."
fields.roofline framing, verbatim: "Figure 1: Roofline analysis for KV cache and Linear weight reads, assuming a Dense LLM with batch B=8, Query heads Q=128, KV heads K=8, head size Hsz=128, and FFN dimension F=65536 running on GB200 NVL72."

title: Mooncake — a multi-node cluster of 8× A800-80GB nodes with intra-node NVLink and inter-node RDMA

fields.hardware requirement: **A compute-node cluster; each node = 8 NVIDIA A800-SXM4-80GB GPUs connected by NVLink, plus RDMA NICs at up to 800 Gbps between nodes; each node runs either a prefill instance or a decoding instance.**
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "During the experiments, the system was deployed on a high-performance computing node cluster to test performance. Each node in the cluster is configured as follows: 8 NVIDIA-A800-SXM4-80GB GPUs, each with 80GB HBM, connected by NVLINK; equipped with RDMA network cards that supporting up to 800 Gbps of interconnect bandwidth between nodes. Each node deploys either a prefill instance or a decoding instance according to the startup parameter."
fields.the disagg cache is also cluster-scoped,: "Mooncake employs a disaggregated architecture that not only separates prefill from decoding nodes, but also groups the CPU, DRAM, SSD, and RDMA resources of the GPU cluster to implement a disaggregated KVCache." - The shipped vLLM connector carries the same RDMA requirement, verbatim (from `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main/docs/features/mooncake_connector_usage.md`): "Mooncake aims to enhance the inference efficiency of large language models (LLMs), especially in slow object storage environments, by constructing a multi-level caching pool on high-speed interconnected DRAM/SSD resources. Compared to traditional caching systems, Mooncake utilizes (GPUDirect) RDMA technology to transfer data directly in a zero-copy manner, while maximizing the use of multi-NIC resources on a single machine." and its shipped two-host example: "python examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py --prefill http://192.168.0.2:8010 --decode http://192.168.0.3:8020"

title: DistServe — 4 nodes × 8 A100-80GB with NVLink, 25 Gbps cross-node

fields.hardware requirement: **4 nodes and 32 GPUs; each node 8× NVIDIA SXM A100-80GB connected with NVLink; requires at least 2 GPUs for the minimum prefill/decode split.**
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "Cluster testbed. We deploy DistServe on a cluster with 4 nodes and 32 GPUs. Each node has 8 NVIDIA SXM A100-80GB GPUs connected with NVLINK. The cross-node bandwidth is 25Gbps. Due to the limited cross-node bandwidth, we use the low node-affinity placement algorithm (§ 2 ) for DistServe in most of the experiments except for the ablation study (§ 6.4 ) which uses simulation."
fields.nvlink/infiniband dependence, verbatim: "While many modern GPU clusters for LLMs are equipped with InfiniBand (e.g., 800 Gbps), in cases where cross-node bandwidth is limited, DistServe relies on the commonly available intra-node NVLINK, where the peak bandwidth between A100 GPUs is 600 GB/s, again rendering the transmission overhead negligible (see § 6.3 ). However, this requirement imposes additional constraints on the placement of prefill and decoding instances that we take into consideration in the next section."
fields.minimum gpu count, verbatim: "Ideally, by allocating 2 GPUs for prefill and 1 GPU for decoding, we can effectively serve the model with an overall goodput of 10 rps, or equally 3.3 rps per GPU, which is 2.1x higher than existing systems."

title: Infinite-LLM — distributed KVCache across a 32× A100 cluster

fields.hardware requirement: **A cluster of 32 A100 GPUs (4 nodes × 8).** The technique is a pooled/distributed GPU-memory KV cache and has no single-GPU mode.

title: MemServe / MemPool — design requires a distributed multi-instance pool; RDMA was never implemented because only one machine was available

fields.hardware requirement: **The design requires multiple serving instances across a cluster with RDMA-capable interconnect. What was actually built and measured is one NVIDIA DGX H800 server with 8× H800-80GB on intra-node NVLink, using NCCL send/recv and sockets instead of RDMA.**
fields.abstract (retrieved by me from the abs p: "We present MemServe, a unified system that integrates both inter-request and intra-request optimizations. MemServe introduces MemPool, an elastic memory pool managing distributed memory and KV caches across serving instances." - §8.1 Setup → "Server." (personally re-verified by me from https://arxiv.org/html/2406.17565v2), verbatim: "We run all tests on a single NVIDIA DGX H800 server. It has 8 H800-80GB GPUs interconnected by NVLink (400GB/s bandwidth). It has 192-core Intel Xeon Platinum CPUs @2.4 GHz and 2 TB DRAM. We use Ubuntu 20.04 with Linux kernel 5.16.7 and CUDA 12.2." - Implementation section — the authors' own statement that the multi-node transport was not built for lack of hardware, verbatim: "MemPool. It has two parts: a Python-based library that exposes API to the inference engine and a C++ core part that executes data transmission. Currently, MemPool uses NCCL's send and recv point-to-point APIs to transmit data between HBM and uses socket API if any side contains DRAM. We have not implemented RDMA-based transmission because we only have a single AI machine."

title: vLLM disaggregated prefill (NIXL / Mooncake connectors) — two instances, RDMA, and MNNVL for the fast cross-node path

fields.hardware requirement: **At least 2 GPUs / 2 vLLM instances; RDMA NICs for the transfer; multi-node NVLink (MNNVL, GB-series) for the peer-memory path.**
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "We implement disaggregated prefilling by running 2 vLLM instances. One for prefill (we call it prefill instance) and one for decode (we call it decode instance), and then use a connector to transfer the prefill KV caches and results from prefill instance to decode instance." - RDMA requirement, verbatim (nixl_connector_usage.md): "In standard disaggregated prefilling, KV cache flows in one direction: Prefill (P) computes the KV cache and Decode (D) reads from P." … "4. D reads KV blocks from P via RDMA (peer-to-peer pull), then generates the response."
fields.mnnvl requirement, verbatim: "GB-series GPUs support multi-node NVLink. NIXL supports this capability, but KVCache must be registered as VMM during KVCache registration. To enable this feature, you need to set `--enable-cumem-allocator` or `--enable-sleep-mode` flags, and set `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL: 'y'` env. Otherwise, NIXL can only use RDMA/TCP for cross-node KVCache transfers." - Cross-node KV lease design, verbatim (`docs/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md`): "In disaggregated prefill/decode deployments, the Prefill instance (P) must hold KV cache blocks in GPU memory after completing a prefill, waiting for the Decode instance (D) to read them via RDMA."

title: vLLM tensor/pipeline parallelism with InfiniBand and GPUDirect RDMA — the multi-node KV-scaling path

fields.hardware requirement: **Multiple GPUs; for multi-node, high-speed network adapters such as InfiniBand plus GPUDirect RDMA.**
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "**Single-node multi-GPU using tensor parallel inference:** if the model is too large for a single GPU but fits on a single node with multiple GPUs, use *tensor parallelism*. For example, set `tensor_parallel_size=4` when using a node with 4 GPUs." … "**Multi-node multi-GPU using tensor parallel and pipeline parallel inference:** if the model is too large for a single node, combine *tensor parallelism* with *pipeline parallelism*. Set `tensor_parallel_size` to the number of GPUs per node and `pipeline_parallel_size` to the number of nodes. For example, set `tensor_parallel_size=8` and `pipeline_parallel_size=2` when using 2 nodes with 8 GPUs per node."
fields.interconnect requirement, verbatim: "Efficient tensor parallelism requires fast internode communication, preferably through high-speed network adapters such as InfiniBand." and "GPUDirect RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) is an NVIDIA technology that allows network adapters to directly access GPU memory, bypassing the CPU and system memory." and "To confirm your InfiniBand card is using GPUDirect RDMA, run vLLM with detailed NCCL logs: `NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE vllm serve ...`." → "If you find `[send] via NET/IB/GDRDMA` in the logs, then NCCL is using InfiniBand with GPUDirect RDMA, which *is* efficient."
fields.nvlink-vs-pp guidance, verbatim: "Furthermore, if the GPUs on the node do not have NVLINK interconnect (e.g. L40S), leverage pipeline parallelism instead of tensor parallelism for higher throughput and lower communication overhead."

title: vLLM — CPU/filesystem KV offloading tier *does* run on one GPU (negative hardware requirement)

fields.hardware requirement: **None beyond one GPU.** Recorded here explicitly because it is the counter-cell: vLLM's `OffloadingConnector`/`TieringOffloadingSpec` offloads KV to CPU pinned memory and secondary tiers with `cudaMemcpyAsync`, with no RDMA, NVLink, or second GPU in the documented path.
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "This guide covers configuration of the [`OffloadingConnector`](disagg_prefill.md), which extends the prefix cache by offloading completed KV blocks to slower but larger tiers (CPU host memory, plus optional secondary tiers) as they are produced. Hits in the offload tiers are promoted back to GPU on demand. Transfers between GPU and CPU use DMA (`cudaMemcpyAsync`) and run asynchronously alongside model computation, so offloading adds minimal CPU- and GPU-core overhead."
fields.single-tier config, verbatim: "`CPUOffloadingSpec` (default): single CPU tier. Completed GPU blocks are copied into pinned host memory." and "Only the CPU primary tier has direct GPU access. Secondary tiers cannot read from or write to GPU memory; all GPU↔secondary transfers are staged through the CPU primary tier." - Its disk tier is explicitly multi-instance-capable on shared storage, verbatim: "KV cache sharing between multiple vLLM instances using the same `root_dir` (e.g., via a shared PVC) works by default: `NONE_HASH` (the chain-hash seed for block content hashes) is derived from a fixed default seed, so identical token content produces identical block filenames across instances."

title: Striped Attention (Ring Attention for causal transformers) — 8× A100-80GB on one NVLink server, or a TPU pod slice

title: NanoCP (2026) — request-level dynamic context parallelism on an H200 cluster with NVLink fabric + 8× 50 GB/s RDMA NICs per node

fields.hardware requirement: **A cluster of NVIDIA H200 GPUs; each node has eight GPUs on a fully-connected NVLink fabric (900 GB/s bidirectional) plus eight 50 GB/s RDMA NICs for inter-node communication. Intra-node payload routing is over NVLink; inter-node is over InfiniBand.** This is the most recent (May 2026) published instance of the multi-GPU-required class.
fields.url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21100 (full HTML v1: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.21100v1), §6.1 Experimental Setup
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "We evaluate NanoCP on a cluster of NVIDIA H200 GPUs. Each node has eight GPUs connected by a fully-connected NVLink fabric (900 GBps bidirectional) and eight 50 GBps RDMA NICs for inter-node communication. We use DeepSeek-V3 ( DeepSeek-AI, 2024a ) and Kimi-K2 ( Team et al., 2025 ) as model backbones."
fields.the routing requirement, verbatim: "the sender transfers the payload directly into the pre-allocated receive buffers of remote instances via NVLink for intra-node routing, or InfiniBand (IB) for inter-node routing ( 2 )."
fields.the cluster scale it targets, verbatim: "In one representative deployment—a 1T-parameter MoE on 32 × H200 with 32DP-32EP—the KV cache capacity of one instance is roughly 1M tokens, already comparable to the context windows of recent models." - Its framing of why the KV cache is the binding constraint, verbatim: "Existing systems bind each request's attention, MoE communication, and KV cache to a single instance. Because attention latency scales with KV cache size while MoE communication latency scales with batch size, this binding cannot balance both simultaneously, producing EP stragglers; it also fragments KV memory across instances, inflating tail latency under long contexts."

title: SGLang session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache

fields.detail: Merged by hzh0425 on 2026-08-02, titled "feat: Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache for agentic multi-turn workloads". This is the single most on-topic shipped artifact for "session-level KV management" and "KV cache growth across multi-turn agentic sessions". The stated motivation: "In multi-turn inference workloads such as agentic workflows and RL rollouts, active sessions accumulate reusable KV prefixes across turns. Under memory pressure, the standard radix cache evicts entries using only the configured cache policy, without considering whether a prefix is still referenced by an active session. This may evict an active session's prefix while unrelated, unreferenced KV remains cached, causing unnecessary recomputation in later turns and reducing cache hit rate and throughput." The mechanism: "Applications pass a stable top-level session_id with each request. When a request finishes, SGLang registers its reusable KV under that session. When the session ends, the application calls /close_session to release those references." Eviction ordering is "(is_referenced, session_ref_count, base_eviction_priority)" with "two LRU passes: unreferenced nodes first, then referenced nodes if more space is required." Importantly it is explicitly not a pin: "Referenced KV is soft-protected, not pinned. If unreferenced KV is insufficient, referenced entries remain evictable." It covers FULL attention ("tracks the reusable prefix path"), SWA ("reusable sliding-window tail") and Mamba ("reusable state at the session frontier").

title: Fine-grained prefix-cache checkpoints at shared-prefix junctions (long system prompts that diverge)

fields.detail: This shipped flag directly targets the "KV reuse across turns with changing system prompts / shared long prefix diverging mid-block" question for hybrid models. The doc states: "Under `--mamba-cache-mode align`, Mamba state is stored only on the Mamba block grid, so a prefix-cache hit can resume only at a block boundary. `--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` also stores a checkpoint at the shared-prefix junction, the point where an earlier request with the same prefix stopped. Requests whose shared prefix ends inside a block can then reuse it." And the workload it is for: "This helps when many requests share a long system prompt and then diverge." Gating: "It is off by default, and takes effect only when all of the following hold: `--mamba-cache-mode align`, EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding on the Mamba group, `--prefix-match-unit` smaller than the Mamba block size, the model does not use multi-module MTP". Confirmed present in the local tree: `vllm/config/cache.py:198  enable_mamba_fine_grained_prefix_cache: bool = False` and `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1302  "--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache"`.

title: vLLM #52041 — skip MM tensor broadcast for prefix-cache-covered items

fields.detail: Merged by njhill 2026-08-19 ("njhill merged 8 commits into vllm-project:main"). The author's framing: "The EngineCore->TP-worker broadcast was designed when request inputs were token IDs (kilobytes), so shipping them unconditionally was both correct and free. Multimodal grafted large tensors onto the same path, but for the classic workload (a fresh image per chat request) the workers genuinely need every tensor, so unconditional shipping remained necessary. What changed recently is multimodal prefix caching". This closes the question of whether prefix-cache-covered payloads can be skipped on the worker broadcast path.

title: AgentKVShift — KV reuse for agentic memory units

fields.detail: Published 2026-05-15 (submitted), cs.AI. Directly addresses "tool-calling KV reuse / retrieval-triggered re-encoding" in agentic memory. Problem statement: "every retrieval triggers a full re-encoding of these structured memory units into Key-Value (KV) states, which dominates prefill latency. Existing training-free KV reuse methods mitigate this by selectively recomputing a small fraction of tokens, but were designed for RAG-style raw passages and degrade on structured agentic memories." title: SideQuest — model-driven KV management for long-horizon agentic reasoning

fields.detail: Published 2026-02-26, cs.AI. Answers "how to bound KV for long chain-of-thought + retrieval-driven agentic loops". The paper states: "In such tasks, the LLM context is dominated by tokens from external retrieval, causing memory usage to grow rapidly and limiting decode performance. While several KV cache compression techniques exist for long-context inputs, we find that existing heuristics fail to support multi-step reasoning models effectively." Method: "we frame KV cache compression as an auxiliary task executed in parallel to the main reasoning task" and "Our evaluations, using a model trained with just 215 samples, show that SideQuest reduces peak token usage by up to 65% on agentic tasks with minimal degradation in accuracy". Full HTML confirms explicit compatibility with the engine's reuse machinery: "ensuring full compatibility with prefix caching to enable efficient context reuse across multiple ReAct iterations", and the serving testbed: "we compare Sidequest against the uncompressed baseline for gpt-oss-20b (Medium Effort) on the FRAMES benchmark using a single NVIDIA H100 GPU."

title: FlowKV — multi-turn isolation for KV compression

fields.detail: Published 2025-05-21, revised v2 2025-10-08, cs.CL. The canonical answer to "repeated compression of early turns destroys multi-turn coherence". Text: "existing eviction strategies often degrade performance by repeatedly compressing early conversational context, leading to information loss and context forgetting. This paper introduces FlowKV, a novel multi-turn isolation mechanism for KV Cache management, which can be applied to any KV Cache compression method without training. FlowKV's core innovation is a multi-turn isolation mechanism that preserves the accumulated compressed KV cache from past turns. Compression is then strategically applied only to the newly generated KV pairs of the latest completed turn, effectively preventing the re-compression of older context and thereby mitigating catastrophic forgetting."

title: EpiCache — episodic KV management for long-term conversation under a fixed budget

fields.detail: Published 2025-09-22, cs.CL. Answers multi-turn LongConvQA under a bounded KV budget without unbounded prefill peak. "EpiCache bounds cache growth through block-wise prefill and preserves topic-relevant context via episodic KV compression, which clusters conversation history into coherent episodes and performs episode-specific KV cache eviction. Across three LongConvQA benchmarks (LongMemEval, Realtalk, and LoCoMo), EpiCache improves accuracy by up to 30%, achieves near full-cache accuracy under 4-6x compression, and reduces latency and peak memory by up to 2.4x and 3.7x, respectively."

title: GrowPage — on-demand KV budgeting that preserves prefix caching

fields.detail: Published 2026-09-03, cs.AI — inside the target window. Answers reasoning/thinking-model KV growth on a single GPU. "GrowPage maintains lightweight dual-timescale query summaries to capture recent and long-term attention behaviors, and uses their relative attention working sets to estimate demand evolution. At each capacity boundary, GrowPage either compresses KV states within the current allocation or acquires an additional physical page when broader demand emerges. By integrating with PagedAttention's page-level memory abstraction, GrowPage preserves continuous batching and prefix caching." Testbed from the full HTML: "All experiments are conducted on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU with 80 GB memory. Following Zipage, we implement GrowPage on nano-vLLM with PagedAttention-based KV management".

title: SAECache — semantic-adaptive prefix-cache eviction with a multi-turn queue

fields.detail: Published 2026-05-12, cs.LG. Answers "which eviction policy should a prefix cache use for agentic/multi-turn traffic". It documents the reuse-rate variance across token roles: "different token types within a prompt, including system prompts, user queries, tool outputs, model responses, and chain-of-thought reasoning, exhibit up to 756x variation in reuse rates, yet no existing eviction policy exploits this signal." Design: "a multi-queue architecture that routes KV blocks to task-specific queues with tailored priority metrics, capturing both session reuse in multi-turn requests and structural reuse in templated single-turn requests". Also records the failure mode of fixed policies: "fixed-parameter alternatives can degrade by up to 2.7x under workload mismatch". It also reports a negative integration result: "Under low-to-moderate concurrency with a single small model, vLLM's aggressive memory management rarely fills the KV cache to capacity, leading to limited eviction activity." Testbed from the HTML: a single NVIDIA A40 GPU, vLLM v0.8.5 (V0 engine), Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.
