title: SAECache — semantic-adaptive prefix cache eviction

fields.detail: Abstract verbatim: "its benefit depends critically on the eviction policy as GPU memory is scarce, and existing policies such as LRU largely treat cached blocks uniformly. This view ignores a fundamental property of LLM prompts: not all tokens are equally worth caching. We show that different token types within a prompt, including system prompts, user queries, tool outputs, model responses, and chain-of-thought reasoning, exhibit up to 756x variation in reuse rates, yet no existing eviction policy exploits this signal." Result verbatim: "we demonstrate that SAECache achieves 1.4x-2.7x TTFT improvement over production-style baselines". See ABANDONED-12 for the negative half of this result.

title: AsymCache / Multi-Segment Attention — lossless KV management with recomputation-cost-aware eviction

fields.detail: Abstract verbatim: "lossless approaches instead evict KV cache blocks from GPU memory and reconstruct them on demand to preserve exact outputs. Existing lossless KV cache management systems primarily base eviction decisions on access frequency or positional heuristics, without considering how different KV cache blocks affect the execution efficiency of GPU attention kernels." Contribution verbatim: "a cache eviction policy that jointly optimizes hit rate and position-aware recomputation cost". Result verbatim: "Experiments show that AsymCache reduces TTFT by up to 1.90-2.03x and time-per-output-token (TPOT) by 1.62-1.71x over latest baselines".

fields.who is still asking: lcc-star (issue author), vLLM

title: Which request should be preempted, and what does the wrong choice cost?

fields.who is still asking: shivasathishs-rp (RFC author), vLLM; implementation in open PR #53723
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "Neither of the current policies takes that into account. FCFS evicts the last request that was admitted, using self.running.pop() . PRIORITY evicts max(running, key=(priority, arrival_time)) . Both ignore how much work a request has already done, so the scheduler can evict a request that has already prefilled several thousand tokens in order to admit a tiny one, and all of that computed KV is discarded." and "I measured how much this costs. I call it the recompute tax, defined as recomputed tokens divided by total token compute. ... The short version is that under KV pressure the tax is large, reaching about 79 percent in a forced offline sweep and 10 to 23 percent in realistic online serving, and a victim-policy ablation shows that the victim choice by itself accounts for roughly half of it." and "Fairness needs attention too. Because LCF evicts the request with the least sunk compute, it tends to pick requests that were only just admitted, so under sustained pressure a request could be preempted again and again and never make progress."
fields.what specifically is missing: a durable, pluggable victim-selection extension point with a fairness contract. Verbatim: "The second part is the actual ask. I would like to promote victim selection to a pluggable extension point under #51608 , which is what its phase 5 anticipates." Open RFC, no close event; the interim `--preemption-victim` implementation is in open PR #53723.

fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "When the unified radix cache evicts a node whose model uses the MAMBA (hybrid-KDA) component, the node is pruned outright from the radix tree instead of being downgraded to host-resident. A subsequent request for the same prefix never even attempts H→D load-back and reports cached_tokens_details=None (no host > 0 hit), even though the backup chain committed pages to the host tier correctly." Root cause, verbatim: "only considers the Full (KV) component when it decides whether a node can stay as an evictable-host leaf ( _evict_host_leaf only checks component_data[FULL].host_value )." Status, verbatim: "Happy to prepare a PR if maintainers want to assign this."
fields.what specifically is missing: host-anchor logic for non-Full components at device-evict time. Open, created 2026-08-05, no close event. A related documented limitation is tracked in SGLang's own docs at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sgl-project/sglang/main/docs/cookbook/autoregressive/InclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash.mdx, verbatim: "Host-memory L2 eviction is not exposed because the KDA cache path is not currently compatible with it. Track the limitation in [issue #33713](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33713)."

title: Admit cached-prefix requests ahead of cold ones within a look-ahead window

fields.who is still asking: fululi12, vLLM
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "The problem is an interaction between strict FCFS admission and prefix caching: a cold request admitted first allocates blocks, and under pressure that allocation evicts blocks which a request further back in the queue still needs. The eviction turns a would-be cache hit into recomputation, and the deeper the shared prefix, the more expensive the loss." Flags proposed, verbatim: "--cache-aware-admission-window N 0 Look-ahead depth over the waiting queue; 0 admits strictly in arrival order" and "--cache-aware-admission-threshold F 0.0 KV cache usage below which the window is not applied". Stated limits, verbatim: "It requires the fcfs policy. Positional reordering is meaningless in a priority heap" and "It requires prefix caching, and is skipped on steps that defer prefill anyway."
fields.what specifically is missing: acceptance/merge; both knobs are "off by default". OPEN PR. A competing SLO-oriented approach is also open (vllm-project/vllm#53571, "[feat]Add SLO-aware scheduling policy", OPEN), and #54625 itself argues they are complementary.

title: Bounded long-context KV in llama.cpp via StreamingLLM-style eviction

fields.who is still asking: jotrujil03, llama.cpp
fields.verbatim quote of the asking: "Long-context generation quickly exhausts VRAM when retaining the entire KV cache. This PR implements StreamingLLM-style KV cache eviction via --kv-evict-sink and --kv-evict-window . By capping the physical cache at sink + recent + n_ubatch cells while allowing the logical context to grow indefinitely, both VRAM footprint and per-token decode latency remain constant over arbitrary sequence lengths." Interaction with the existing lifetime mechanism, verbatim: "Compatibility : Disables context shifting ( get_can_shift = false )." Reported result, verbatim: "Wikitext-2 perplexity remains stable (~6.31 baseline vs. ~6.48 with a 1024-token window), while decode throughput stays flat across long sequences."
fields.what specifically is missing: acceptance. OPEN PR (created 2026-08-23), and the bot flagged process problems ("PR Template not respected", "AI-generated content: While code is allowed to be generated by AI, please write the PR description and commit messages on your own"). Related open llama.cpp proposals for the same memory-pressure problem: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28046 ("Add per-entry prompt-cache context limit"), https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28092 ("server : add --cache-disk for a persistent prompt cache"), https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28267 ("Option to quant KV cache to q8_0 lazily (i.e. when fp16 cache fills up)") — all OPEN.

title: Reclaiming the prefill-activation reserve with an elastic KV cache — honest negative result

fields.closure status: published paper whose own central result is negative — the mechanism works, the premise does not pay off
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "Having built the mechanism, we test the premise it rests on and report an honest negative result. It only pays off if a small prefill chunk size badly hurts prefill latency. In a controlled experiment injecting long prompts into a live decode load, that penalty is small (median time-to-first-token differs by about 1% between chunk sizes of 8192 and 32768 tokens), because prefill is compute bound and decode consumes only about one token per sequence per step. Simply lowering max_num_batched_tokens recovers more KV than the controller does, at nearly equal latency. The reserve also dilutes under tensor parallelism, from 16% of KV at TP1 to 2.7% at TP4. We state precisely when reclaiming the reserve could still help, and release the mechanism as a reusable userspace elastic-VMM allocator."
fields.note: the mechanism itself still shipped as an artifact — abstract verbatim: "It is pure userspace on the CUDA virtual-memory path: two physical handles mapped into one contiguous virtual range per layer, so the attention kernel is unchanged and no driver patch is required. ... A static commit of the same memory is unsafe, crashing on prefill bursts, which makes the dynamic toggle necessary."

title: CPU swap-based preemption in vLLM (and a later per-layer SwapConnector revival)

fields.who: vLLM project (removal by majiayu000, superseding an earlier abandoned PR by mcelrath); SwapConnector attempt by ZehaoLu98
fields.closure status: (a) feature deleted — `--swap-space` removed, `swap_space` field removed; (b) the later per-layer swap connector PR closed unmerged by its author the same day it was opened
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "In the V1 engine, num_cpu_blocks is hardcoded to 0 ( v1/engine/core.py:287 ), confirming swap space was never allocated or used. Picks up the abandoned PR #27988 as suggested by @DarkLight1337 in #27984 ." (PR #36216 body) — and, from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/design/metrics.md: "Two legacy metrics relate to a \"swapped\" preemption mode that is no longer relevant in v1: - `vllm:num_requests_swapped` - `vllm:cpu_cache_usage_perc` In this mode, when a request was preempted (e.g. to make room in KV cache to complete other requests), kv cache blocks were swapped out to CPU memory. The `--swap-space` flag has been removed as this feature is no longer used in V1." and "This proved to be a better option than CPU swapping since blocks can be evicted slowly on demand and the part of the prompt that was evicted can be recomputed." For the revival attempt, the only closure evidence on the page is the timeline line "ZehaoLu98 closed this Mar 1, 2026" (opened 2026-03-01, closed the same day, `"state":"CLOSED"`, `mergedBy: null`); no closing comment or maintainer reason is present, so no reason is quoted.

fields.note: this is the direct answer to the "preemption: recompute vs swap" question for the target stack — vLLM V1 chose recompute and deleted the swap machinery.

title: Soft-pinning recently-hit prefix-cache entries to stop cache collapse

fields.closure status: CLOSED unmerged by the author (human, not a bot; not a maintainer decision)
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "Closing this too — same reasoning as #43302 (close comment). @stecasta's block-pool instrumentation on the #42948 thread (comment) shows the real bug is 131% pool overflow from the homogeneous lcm=256 physical block layout vs DSv4-Flash's {256, 64, 4, 8}-block-size KV groups. Under that overflow, some eviction every alloc cycle is mandatory; the recent-hit set in this PR can only delay the eviction of blocks that have already served a lookup hit, which by itself doesn't help the agentic-rotation case (per @stecasta's BS-sweep: 46% at BS=4, 21% at BS=8 — meaningful mitigation but not a fix). The real avenue is heterogeneous per-page-size pools so the bs=4 SWA indexer stops costing 64× its useful storage: #42082 (RFC) + #42374 (WIP). Closing this PR rather than leaving a workaround in the review queue. Thanks to everyone who looked at the earlier iterations. Refs: #42948, #42082, #42374."

title: Attention-sink-protected eviction policy request

fields.closure status: CLOSED (completed) by the issue author himself after a collaborator's clarification — a withdrawn request, not a maintainer rejection
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "Thanks for the quick clarification — you're right, and I should have read the block manager more carefully before opening this. vLLM only evicts free blocks, so sink tokens in active sequences are never at risk. The concern I was modeling (early token eviction corrupting attention distribution) applies to sliding-window KV cache modes like StreamingLLM, which vLLM doesn't implement. For standard PagedAttention, this is a non-issue. The underlying analysis (identifying sink tokens and spike channels) is still useful for quantization — knowing which hidden-state channels are outliers helps bitsandbytes/AWQ configs avoid clipping them. But that's a separate, narrower topic and doesn't belong in a KV eviction issue. Closing this. Apologies for the noise."
fields.note: the clarification it responds to, verbatim from collaborator `noooop`: "As far as I know, vLLM only evicts free blocks, meaning blocks that are not being used by any running requests. So what is the relationship between free blocks and attention sink tokens, since no requests are using them?"

title: Region-aware eviction decays — self-undercutting limitation

fields.closure status: published paper whose own abstract undercuts part of the technique
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "Accumulated-attention retention performs better on unpinned content, however, and ablations identify attention-score normalization as the main limitation of the current formulation. These results establish semantic prompt structure as a robust signal for KV-cache management while clarifying how it should be combined with attention-based importance."
fields.note: the paper's positive half is real and quantified, verbatim: "Across all settings, attention lifetimes differ by an order of magnitude across regions: system-token half-lives range from 148 to 189 decoding steps, compared with 14 to 16 for scratchpad tokens. Pinning preserves system-region facts at full-cache accuracy in every setting, while no baseline preserves more than 13 of 24. Region-aware retention remains effective as context grows, whereas recency-based retention collapses."

title: CacheTTL's own TTL cost model under distribution shift

fields.who: Continuum/CacheTTL authors (arXiv 2511.02230), "Appendix D Limitations and Future Work"
fields.closure status: published paper's own limitations section undercutting the TTL derivation (not a retraction — a scoped failure mode)
fields.stated reason, verbatim: "Sensitivity of the TTL Cost Model: CacheTTL relies on a cost–benefit model that combines empirical tool-call CDFs, memory-usage estimates, and a "memoryfulness" factor to derive optimal TTL values. While this design is principled, it assumes that tool-call distributions and workload characteristics are sufficiently stable for historical samples to be predictive. In highly volatile or adversarial workloads, such as agents whose tool latencies abruptly shift due to back-end contention or external API variability, the model may produce suboptimal TTLs, temporarily degrading scheduling efficiency. ... We leave handling sudden distribution shifts in agent as future work."

fields.hardware requirement: inherits the multi-instance migration model it extends; evaluation is simulation-based (Vidur) rather than on one GPU
fields.verbatim evidence of the requirement: "Llumnix introduced a dynamic, migration-capable multi-instance scheduler for LLM inference that achieves load balancing, defragmentation, prioritization, and auto-scaling through a unified \"freeness\" metric. However, Llumnix's priority model is restricted to two levels (high and normal), an abstraction too coarse to express the richer SLA classes common in production deployments. In this work, we extend Llumnix's priority model to support an arbitrary number of tiers and evaluate the effects of this extension under three realistic priority distributions (uniform, Gaussian, enterprise) using Vidur, a high-fidelity LLM inference simulator."
